name: Tridentopsis

project_scope.selection_mode: Two manifest-backed species; compare accepted Tridentopsis concepts without installing taxa
project_scope.source_pool_crosswalk: The live Master Plant Pool still indexes these two under Tridens; they are already installed as accepted Tridentopsis species. Do not create duplicate cards. Tridens eragrostoides is a separate unresolved historical source-pool name and is NOT silently included in this two-species comparison.
project_scope.native_range_guardrail: Both canonical records retain provisional target-zone range labels and remain excluded from confirmed-native metrics.

look_here_first: On a mature flowering stem, inspect the WHOLE PANICLE before looking at color: widely separated, spreading branches and an open, broadly ovate outline suggest T. buckleyana; closely ascending branches making a very narrow, nearly spike-like panicle suggest T. mutica. Then count florets on several intact spikelets and inspect the three-veined lemma under magnification.
shared_genus_traits: Warm-season perennial grasses with sheathed leaves, a ligule at the blade/sheath junction, and panicles of laterally compressed multi-flowered spikelets.
Each floret is enclosed by a lemma and palea; outer glumes remain distinguishable. Both species have three-veined lemmas and can show basal lemma pubescence.
Use whole panicle architecture, spikelet anatomy and measured reproductive characters together; flower or spikelet color alone is not diagnostic.

species_comparison_matrix.buckleyana: Open, ovate panicle with ascending to spreading, visibly separated primary branches; 10–28 cm long (GrassBase via Kew).
species_comparison_matrix.mutica: Strongly contracted panicle with erect, closely appressed branches; 7–20(25) cm long, about 0.3–0.8 cm wide (FNA treatment).
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Same-scale intact mature panicles with branch angles and width annotated.

species_comparison_matrix.buckleyana: Stiff straight branches, often 4–13 cm long, with distant spikelets (GrassBase via Kew).
species_comparison_matrix.mutica: Short erect/appressed branches, with spikelets imbricate but generally not crowded; pedicels ~1–2 mm (FNA).

species_comparison_matrix.buckleyana: Usually 3–5 fertile florets; a reduced distal floret may be present (GrassBase via Kew).
species_comparison_matrix.confidence: high but ranges touch at 5; count multiple intact spikelets
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Dissected whole spikelets with individual florets numbered.
Side-by-side spikelets aligned against a millimeter ruler.

species_comparison_matrix.buckleyana: Three-veined, 4–6 mm lemma; pubescence described along basal midvein and lower margins (GrassBase via Kew).
species_comparison_matrix.mutica: Lemmas 3.5–7 mm; midvein hairy along basal 1/3–1/2 and lateral veins hairy well above midlength (FNA).
species_comparison_matrix.confidence: microscopic supporting character; exact overlap and mounting orientation require diagnostic review
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Matched dorsal lemma macros at ~10–20×, with midvein and lateral veins labeled.

species_comparison_matrix.buckleyana: Ciliate membranous ligule about 0.4–1 mm; blades 1–4 mm wide (GrassBase via Kew).
species_comparison_matrix.mutica: Ciliate membranous ligule about 0.5–1 mm; blades 1–4 mm wide, often involute or loosely infolded (FNA).
species_comparison_matrix.confidence: overlapping; genus confirmation, NOT a species key
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Matched collar/ligule macros with mm scale and blade cross-section.

species_comparison_matrix.buckleyana: Tufted perennial; culms reported 40–80 cm (GrassBase via Kew).
species_comparison_matrix.mutica: Tufted, knotty shortly rhizomatous base; culms 20–80 cm (FNA).
species_comparison_matrix.confidence: supporting only; culm height overlaps and base needs careful observation
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Whole-plant basal crown and node/sheath detail.

quick_comparison_steps: Confirm grass anatomy at a node and ligule, then isolate a true multi-flowered spikelet.
Photograph the entire mature panicle from the side; open/spreading vs tightly contracted is the primary split.
Count fertile florets on three intact spikelets; 3–4 supports buckleyana, 6–11 supports mutica; a count of 5 is not decisive.
Measure spikelet length, but do not use 8–10 mm as a standalone decision.
Dissect a mature floret and label the three lemma veins and hair placement; leave an uncertain specimen at Tridentopsis sp. rather than force a name.
overlap_and_cautions: Both species are perennial bunchgrasses; height, blade width, ligule length, purple tinge, and spikelet length overlap.

T. buckleyana's existing provisional species card calls the inflorescence 'compact' and 'fluffy', whereas the detailed GrassBase/Kew description gives an open, ovate panicle with separated branches. Treat this as a targeted card-level morphology discrepancy for Taxonomy + Diagnostic Review; the genus lesson uses the cited panicle architecture and does not silently edit the species card.
The source pool's Tridens buckleyanus and Tridens muticus are historical names for these canonical species, not additional learner taxa.
T. mutica's base may be shortly rhizomatous; do not infer species from apparent rhizomes in a partial or damaged specimen.
Some old references place these taxa in Tridens; compare accepted names and morphological descriptions, not just the historical genus label.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.separation: A contracted panicle can mimic T. mutica; inspect spikelet florets, glumes and three-veined lemma pubescence; use the existing Tridens genus comparison rather than relying on narrow panicle alone.
Open branching can mimic T. buckleyana; inspect the exposed basal portions of flexuous panicle branches and the relative glume/lemma length, as taught in the Tridens module.
A much larger, broadly open panicle and often flattened basal sheaths support T. flavus; check spikelet anatomy when panicles are immature.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.status: historical Master Plant Pool name; taxonomy mapping unresolved here
local_source_pool_lookalikes.separation: Do not treat as a third Tridentopsis species without a separate accepted-name/concept review.
Use dissected multi-flowered spikelets, glume proportions, lemma venation and panicle branching, not purple coloration.

curation_status.genus_lesson: four anatomy roles and three comparison cards added; prior comparison matrix and scientific caveats preserved

anatomy_lessons.look: Photograph the entire mature head against a ruler; note how far primary branches spread from the axis.
anatomy_lessons.species_comparison: Published descriptions: T. buckleyana generally open/ovate (10–28 cm long); T. mutica tightly contracted (7–20(25) cm long). The provisional buckleyana card's compact/fluffy wording is under scientific review.

anatomy_lessons.plain: The grass flowering unit and the individual florets inside
anatomy_lessons.look: Dissect several intact spikelets and count fertile florets, then measure length in mm.
anatomy_lessons.species_comparison: T. buckleyana typically 3–5 fertile florets; T. mutica 5–11; five florets and 8–10 mm spikelet lengths overlap.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: paired dissected spikelets with mm ruler

anatomy_lessons.plain: The outer bract around a single grass floret
anatomy_lessons.look: Use a hand lens or macro to find three veins and where hairs run along the central and lateral veins.
anatomy_lessons.species_comparison: Hair distribution is supporting only until regional keys and matched specimens are reconciled.

anatomy_lessons.plain: Tiny tissue at the joint of leaf blade and sheath
anatomy_lessons.look: Open the blade-sheath junction; show the ciliate membranous ligule and measure its length.
anatomy_lessons.species_comparison: Both commonly ~0.5–1 mm; helps recognize anatomy but does not split these species.

comparison_cards.title: Whole panicle silhouette
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Open, separated branches versus strongly contracted near-spike outline.
comparison_cards.caution: The buckleyana species-card discrepancy remains unresolved; don't force ID from one partial head.

comparison_cards.title: Floret counts and spikelet lengths
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Count 3–5 versus 5–11 florets in multiple mature spikelets and measure against mm scale.
comparison_cards.caution: Five florets and 8–10 mm lengths overlap.

comparison_cards.title: Lemma hairs and ligule
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Check three-veined lemma hair placement; use ligule to confirm grass structures.
comparison_cards.caution: Do not rely on shared short ciliate ligules or unverified pubescence claims alone.
